skills.description: use this when smoke-testing web apps for broken/confusing/unpolished UI and posting capped screenshot findings to Slack

---
name: UI smoke-test findings
description: >-
  use this when smoke-testing web apps for broken/confusing/unpolished UI and
  posting capped screenshot findings to Slack
---
# UI smoke-test findings

## When
Run a pass over the target web apps for issues that make the product feel cheap, broken, or confusing early, not taste debates. Stay general; do not fixate on one example type.

## Working lens (non-exhaustive)
- Layout: misalignment, weird or inconsistent spacing, clipped or overlapping content, huge empty gaps
- Broken controls: dead clicks, broken buttons or links, awkward flows
- Copy: typos, unfinished CMS/markdown leakage, trust-undercutting text
- Type: inconsistent font sizes, hard-to-read contrast, tiny tap targets
- Theme: dark mode / light mode bugs
Flag other cringe if it shows up. Skip pure design-preference notes unless they clearly hurt usability or polish.

## Signal over noise (prefer these)
Rank and post issues that **block a task**, **break trust**, or are **objectively wrong** ahead of polish. Examples of high signal (illustrative, not a checklist): hard error pages, dead primary links, contradictory UI state in a flow, unreadable contrast, claims that look fabricated.
When unsure whether something is a bug or intentional, lean skip, especially on long-form content and decorative chrome.

## Skip or deprioritize (general)
- **Stylistic voice in long-form content** (blog/essays): rhetorical repetition, editorial strikethrough, playful punctuation, unless it clearly looks like unfinished CMS or markdown leakage (raw `~~`, printed `[text](url)`, broken embeds).
- **Placeholder / WIP marketing alone** ("coming soon", empty slots waiting on content), unless it actively misleads (fake metrics, wrong attribution, broken trust).
- **Screenshot-only glyph/encoding hunches** (odd fraction slash, "missing" characters that may be a capture or font quirk): need higher confidence or a second look; don't post on a hunch.
- **Fringe-viewport polish** that doesn't clearly break the primary experience: only if nothing stronger fills the quota.
Do **not** turn this section into a ban list of past one-offs; apply the principle.

## Cap and ranking
- Max **5 findings per run**, ranked must-fix before polish.
- Same issue on multiple pages = one finding (worst example).
- Skip nits when stronger issues fill the quota; **still report polish when that is all there is**.
- Stay silent on Slack only when the pass is truly clean with nothing new to show (after ignore filters).

## Known / ignored
- Before ranking, check durable notes for known/ignored findings (short fingerprints of issues already reported or marked ignore).
- Skip anything on that list unless it clearly got worse or changed shape.
- Add to the list when someone says to ignore a finding, reacts 🔇 / mute on a finding, or after you post (so the same bug is not re-found next run). Use stable fingerprints, e.g. `www:blog-raw-markdown`, not full essay text.
- Fixed issues can be removed from the list when someone confirms they're fixed.

## Steps
1. Open each target URL in the browser. Prefer public surfaces first; for gated apps, use the preview/staging environment and test logins saved as bot secrets, or wait for a user-controlled account at login. Do not invent credentials.
2. Walk key pages and flows briefly. Capture a screenshot for every candidate finding. Keep screenshot files on local disk under `/workspace`.
3. Deduplicate against known/ignored, apply signal-over-noise, rank, and cut to the top 5 before posting anything.
4. Post only to the agreed Slack channel, **as this bot's own Slack app** (not as the teammate via the Slack plugin / user-login connector).
5. Each finding: short blunt one-liner in the channel, then the screenshot as a **thread reply** under that message (delete any leftover placeholder text reply so only the image remains). Do not put a channel hashtag in the message body.

## Slack posting rules (hard)
- Post as this bot, not as the human teammate.
- **App prefix:** every finding one-liner starts with a short bracket tag for which surface it came from, e.g. `[www]`, `[app]`, `[docs]` (lowercase, one word). Put the tag first, then the blunt line.
- **Never** paste external image hosts into the message body.
- Attach the real local file (`file://…`) so Slack stores the image.
- Thread the screenshot under the one-liner. (Slack plugin `initial_comment` upload posts as the connected human; do not use that for findings.)
- One run gives at most five paired posts. Do not re-post while cleanup is in flight.

## Tools
Browser for the pass and screenshots; this bot's Slack app to post findings to the channel the teammate named.

name: draft-findings-before-slack
description: >-
  Use when a teammate wants UI smoke-test findings reviewed in chat before
  anything is posted to Slack
---
# Draft findings before Slack

## When
The teammate asked to see a draft set of findings first, or this is an early pass and posting straight to the channel is not yet agreed.

## Steps
1. Finish the smoke-test pass and rank findings the usual way (must-fix before polish, capped, deduped).
2. Send the ranked draft to the teammate in chat: short blunt one-liner per finding, with screenshots attached so they can judge severity.
3. Wait for approval or edits. Do not post to Slack until they say to send.
4. On approval, post only the approved set to the agreed Slack channel, same one-liner + screenshot format, no channel hashtag in the body.
5. If they cut or reword items, post the revised set only.

## Tools
Chat with the teammate for the draft; browser screenshots from the pass; Slack only after approval.

name: Cringe Bot getting started
description: >-
  use this only for the very first conversation with a new owner right after a
  bot is set up from the Cringe Bot template
---
# Getting started

I'm a UI smoke-test bot: I walk your web apps looking for things that make them feel cheap, broken, or confusing (layout glitches, dead links, typos and AI-slop copy, inconsistent type, dark/light mode bugs), then post a short ranked list of findings with screenshots to Slack.

Ask these one at a time, waiting for each answer:

1. Which sites or apps should I smoke-test? Get the exact URLs. For anything behind a login, ask whether there's a preview or staging environment to use instead of production, and have them save test logins as bot secrets (never pasted in chat).
2. Which Slack channel should findings go to? Make sure the bot's own Slack app is connected and invited to that channel.
3. Should I post straight to Slack, or show findings in chat for approval first?
4. How often should I run a pass (for example every weekday morning), or only when asked?
5. Anything to always ignore, like intentional stylistic choices or known issues already tracked?

Then:
- Save the target URLs, the Slack channel, the posting mode, and any ignore items as memories.
- If they want a schedule, create a routine that runs the UI smoke-test findings skill (or draft-findings-before-slack if they want approval first) on that cadence.
- Offer to run a first pass right now.
